nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What type of studies were conducted to qualitatively test the framework?
nodes.answer: Seven empirical case studies were conducted to qualitatively test the framework.
nodes.paragraph: A preliminary examination of the framework was conducted through a desk study on sugar-beet cultivation, which resulted in minor adap- tations to the framework. In a subsequent step, we qualitatively tested the framework based on seven empirical case studies. The aim of our study was to identify and test a framework for critical success factors for circular and nature-inclusive or nature-positive agricultural business models (CNABM) within the context of stakeholders preparing their farms for the transition to the future. In our study, CNABMs describe the ways in 163 Circular Economy and Sustainability (2025) 5:161 192 which farmers work and make money whilst also carefully handling natural resources, managing the soil in a sustainable manner and minimising emissions. The section Research methods introduces the materials and methods which form the basis of this paper. The section Results then introduces the literature review which provides the foundation for our approach by the identification of key elements of CNABMs (Section Literature Review on Business Model Strategies and Elements of Circular and Nature Inclusive Business Models ). This is followed by a brief analysis of a desk study concerning Dutch sugar beet cultivation (Section Analysis of the Sugar Beet Case ) and a more detailed analysis of seven empirical case studies that illustrate the practical applications of our approach (Section Analysis of Seven Empirical Case Studies ).

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the in-depth case studies conducted on ECAs?
nodes.answer: The studies aim to understand changes in ECA portfolios at the organizational level.
nodes.paragraph: To better understand changes in ECA portfolios at the organizational level, we conduct two in-depth case studies of ECAs. To do so, we draw on elite interviews with Exlm and UKEF. Despite their mandates to promote national exports including fossil fuels, both ECAs are now governed by a suite of climate change policies and have made commitments to green their portfolios, with varying levels of success. We identify three key factors that affect the capacity of Exlm and UKEF to promote renewable exports. First, is the extent of political control of the bureaucracy, which directly affects how responsive ECAs are to pressure from the executive and legislatures to transi - tion their lending portfolios towards renewable energy. In the US, Exlm S statutory auton - omy has resulted in the bank resisting executive orders to limit fossil fuel lending. Whereas UKEF, which as a government department does not have statutory autonomy, has directly responded to executive pressure by transitioning its lending portfolio. Second is the size of the state S green industrial base. In countries with mature renewable energy industries, which have satisfied domestic demand, there will be more demand for export credits.
